A course evaluation in which students rate each part of a course on 1 grid, compared between students who took it in person and online. surveyframe gives you the questionnaire, the analysis plan and a report for the teaching team.

## Preview the questionnaire

This is the questionnaire as respondents see it. It is a preview, so answers go nowhere. [Open it in a new tab](../../studies/matrix_likert/preview.html).

```{=html}
<iframe src="../../studies/matrix_likert/preview.html" title="Preview of the Course evaluation survey questionnaire" style="width:100%;height:560px;border:1px solid #d9e2ec;border-radius:6px"></iframe>
```

## The analysis plan, ready to preregister

Before any data is collected, surveyframe writes the pre-analysis plan: the study, the questionnaire, each research question with its hypotheses, method and decision rule, and what a preregistration still asks for. [Read the plan](../../studies/matrix_likert/plan.html), or [download the instrument (.sframe)](../../studies/matrix_likert/matrix_likert.sframe) and open it in SurveyStudio.

Methods it declares: Descriptive statistics, Frequencies and percentages, Cross-tabulation.

## Start in 2 steps (no coding)

1. Install surveyframe in R: `install.packages("surveyframe")`
2. In RStudio, open the Addins menu, choose **surveyframe: Try a demo**, and pick `matrix_likert`. The study opens in SurveyStudio.

## Questions

### Can I change the parts of the course?

Yes. Edit the rows of the grid in SurveyStudio's Design screen. Each row becomes its own column in the data.

### Can students answer anonymously?

Yes. The questionnaire asks for no name, and the respondent id is generated, not entered.

### How do I collect the answers?

Download the survey as 1 HTML file from the Collect screen and share it, with a free Google Sheet collecting the answers.

## For R users

```{=html}
<details><summary>Open this study in R</summary>
```

```r
d <- sframe_demo("matrix_likert")
render_report(d$instrument)                 # the pre-analysis plan
results <- run_analysis_plan(d$responses, d$instrument)
```
